title: Icariside II suppresses Enterovirus 71 replication via blockade of NF-kappaB p65 activation.
authors: Xie, Jiarong; Shi, Bin; Liu, Zhengyun; Luo, Guo; Wang, Huan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Icariside II抑制肠道病毒71型复制，涉及NF-kappaB通路和分子对接，但核心是病毒-宿主蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Enterovirus 71 (EV71) infection remains a serious public health threat without a specific antiviral drug. Icariside II (ICS II), a natural active compound, has shown various pharmacological effects. This study aims to evaluate the anti-EV71 activity of ICS II and to decipher whether the NF-kappaB pathway, a key signaling mediator in viral pathogenesis, is involved in its mechanism of action. Firstly, the cytotoxicity of ICS II was assessed by CCK-8 assay to determine its maximal non-cytotoxic concentration. The antiviral efficacy of ICS II was determined by assessing cytopathic effect (CPE), viral titer (Reed-Muench method), and viral VP1 protein expression (Western blot and qRT-PCR) in EV71-infected human rhabdomyosarcoma (RD) cells. Network pharmacology prediction, molecular docking, and drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) assays were integrated to identify the key interacting target. Immunofluorescence and Western blot were performed to evaluate NF-kappaB p65 nuclear translocation. ELISA was performed to determine the concentrations of inflammatory cytokines. The results showed that ICS II exhibited significant anti-EV71 activity at a non-cytotoxic concentration (10 muM), markedly reducing CPE, viral titer, and VP1 expression. We identified NF-kappaB p65 as a key interacting target of ICS II, and demonstrated that ICS II effectively impeded EV71-induced NF-kappaB p65 nuclear translocation. Accordingly, treatment with ICS II markedly reduced the levels of the inflammatory cytokines IL-1beta, IL-6, and TNF-alpha. Our study reveals that the anti-EV71 activity of ICS II is potentially associated with modulation of NF-kappaB p65, providing mechanistic insights into the antiviral effects of this natural product.
abstract_zh: 肠道病毒71型（EV71）感染仍然是一个严重的公共卫生威胁，目前尚无特异性抗病毒药物。淫羊藿次苷II（ICS II）作为一种天然活性化合物，已显示出多种药理作用。本研究旨在评估ICS II的抗EV71活性，并探讨NF-kappaB通路（病毒发病机制中的关键信号介质）是否参与其作用机制。首先，通过CCK-8实验评估ICS II的细胞毒性，以确定其最大无细胞毒性浓度。在EV71感染的人横纹肌肉瘤（RD）细胞中，通过评估细胞病变效应（CPE）、病毒滴度（Reed-Muench法）和病毒VP1蛋白表达（Western blot和qRT-PCR）来确定ICS II的抗病毒效力。整合网络药理学预测、分子对接和药物亲和力响应靶标稳定性（DARTS）实验，以识别关键相互作用靶点。通过免疫荧光和Western blot评估NF-kappaB p65的核转位。通过ELISA测定炎症细胞因子的浓度。结果表明，ICS II在无细胞毒性浓度（10 μM）下表现出显著的抗EV71活性，显著减少CPE、病毒滴度和VP1表达。我们确定NF-kappaB p65为ICS II的关键相互作用靶点，并证明ICS II有效阻碍EV71诱导的NF-kappaB p65核转位。相应地，ICS II处理显著降低了炎症细胞因子IL-1β、IL-6和TNF-α的水平。我们的研究揭示，ICS II的抗EV71活性可能与其调节NF-kappaB p65相关，为这种天然产物的抗病毒效应提供了机制性见解。
